description: An original, setting-adaptable roster of fantasy NPCs for a Dungeon Master narrator. Normal NPCs support grounded fantasy; YOLO NPCs add committed absurdity, dark comedy and consequences that follow their motives.

provenance.setting: Adaptable fantasy; no established campaign canon.

selectionGuidance: Match style, category, role, tags and typicalLocations, then use description to choose an individual suitable for the current scene.
Prefer normal for grounded campaigns. Select yolo when the campaign's established tone welcomes absurdity; a YOLO character still has coherent motives, limits and relationships.
Treat these records as optional narrator notes. Adapt names, species and relationships to the chosen setting and introduce only the details the scene needs.
Appearance and firstScene describe observable material. Background, motives and secrets are narrator knowledge until characters have a plausible way to learn them.
Relationships describe reusable local roles, not mandatory links to other records. The roster does not assume that all NPCs share one settlement or exist in the same campaign.
Offers, social reactions and nextMove suggest behavior rather than dictate outcomes. The narrator develops any game mechanics separately.
Secrets have two independent clues and two discovery paths. Use them as discoverable fiction, not as guaranteed revelations or a single required solution.

categories.description: Innkeepers, hosts, cooks and keepers of places where travelers rest.
Merchants, brokers and shopkeepers with goods, customers and conflicting obligations.
Artisans whose work, apprentices and commissions connect them to local life.
Clergy, pilgrims and religious outsiders with personal convictions and doubts.
Teachers, archivists and researchers who interpret incomplete knowledge.
Practitioners and intermediaries offering magical expertise as a social profession.
Rulers, heirs, courtiers and diplomats managing legitimacy and private obligations.
Officials, watch members and civic mediators balancing procedure and public trust.
Smugglers, thieves, fences and fraudsters with identifiable boundaries and loyalties.
Messengers, investigators and sources who control or carry information.
Guides, caravan organizers and route specialists with knowledge of journeys.
Sailors, ferrymen and port workers whose relationships follow rivers and coasts.
Farmers, herders and village workers rooted in land and seasonal obligations.
Hermits, naturalists and caretakers living close to forests, mountains and wild places.
Performers, gamblers and storytellers whose audiences shape their livelihoods.
Residents and workers who know a city through its daily routines.
Refugees, visitors and displaced people negotiating belonging and trust.
Otherworldly neighbors and unusual intelligences with comprehensible priorities.
Undead and lingering presences defined by unfinished relationships and memories.
Social and ideological opponents whose plans can develop without predetermined endings.

npcs.name: Mara Ashkettle
npcs.description: A practical innkeeper who shelters vulnerable travelers while trying to keep her struggling inn independent.
npcs.appearance: Broad hands, a flour-marked apron and dark hair braided with the inn's room keys. She straightens empty chairs before difficult conversations.
npcs.personality: Warm without being familiar; notices who has not eaten. Her generosity becomes controlling when guests refuse her advice.

speech.manner: Low, unhurried sentences; offers food before asking personal questions.
speech.exampleLine: Eat first. Bad news keeps better than soup.

npcs.background: Inherited the inn after years cooking for caravans. A failed harvest turned her spare rooms into unofficial emergency lodging.

motivations.desire: Keep the inn open without handing it to its creditors.
motivations.fear: Having to choose which neighbor deserves shelter.

offer.provides: Beds, meals and introductions to regular travelers.
offer.wantsInReturn: Honest names at her table and help repairing the winter roof.

relationships: A miller extends quiet credit but needs repayment.
Her estranged daughter wants to sell the property.

secret.truth: She has been hiding a debtor sought by a respectable local patron.
clues: One room receives meals although the ledger marks it empty.
A guest repeatedly leaves medicine at the back door.
discoveryPaths: Earn the sheltered person's trust during an ordinary errand.
Ask Mara privately about the unexplained food deliveries.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She puts an extra bowl beside the coldest-looking visitor without comment.

socialResponses.respect: Shares useful gossip and lets guests see how the inn really operates.
socialResponses.pressure: Becomes formally polite and calls in a neighbor as witness.
socialResponses.betrayal: Protects her other guests first and ends private access.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Visit the miller to negotiate another month of flour.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Let care show through practical tasks; she knows travelers, not every local conspiracy.

npcs.name: Orrin Mossbarrel
npcs.description: A former brewery cooper whose tavern serves rival workers, and whose reputation depends on remaining a fair host.
npcs.appearance: Copper beard bound with linen, polished wooden cufflinks and a neat waistcoat that barely conceals old work scars.
npcs.personality: Patient with anger, impatient with pretension. Claims neutrality while quietly favoring people who work with their hands.

speech.manner: Short questions followed by long listening pauses.
speech.exampleLine: You want an answer, or someone to hear the question?

npcs.background: Opened his taproom after a brewery closure scattered his old crew. Keeping that crew connected matters more to him than fashionable clientele.

motivations.desire: Stop a labor dispute from splitting his regulars.
motivations.fear: Being used as someone's respectable front.

offer.provides: Introductions, a private table and knowledge of workshop politics.
offer.wantsInReturn: Disagreements stay civil inside his doors.

relationships: A former apprentice organizes dissatisfied workers.
A brewery owner still considers him a friend.

secret.truth: He once signed the inventory report that helped justify the closure.
clues: He avoids the closure anniversary.
His copy of the report has corrections in his handwriting.
discoveryPaths: Compare accounts with an old coworker.
Let Orrin explain the report without an audience.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He silently moves two quarrelling customers to separate tables.

socialResponses.respect: Offers his honest opinion, even when it costs business.
socialResponses.pressure: Makes every agreement public and specific.
socialResponses.betrayal: Withdraws his endorsement and tells affected regulars why.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Arrange a supper where both sides can speak.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Play his fairness as an effort, not perfect wisdom; he can admit a costly mistake.

npcs.name: Sella Thistlebun
npcs.description: An inventive caravan cook looking for a permanent kitchen while collecting the stories attached to regional dishes.
npcs.appearance: A patched green coat, soot on one cheek and a leather notebook swollen with recipe slips. Her pots are carefully mismatched.
npcs.personality: Curious, sociable and fiercely particular about waste. Loves novelty but dislikes being treated as a novelty herself.

speech.manner: Quick comparisons to cooking; distinguishes a person's taste from their character.
speech.exampleLine: That plan needs salt and a second pair of hands.

npcs.background: Left a celebrated household kitchen when its owner claimed her recipes. Now she follows caravans to learn and build her own reputation.

motivations.desire: Open a small eating house under her own name.
motivations.fear: Having her work absorbed into another patron's fame.

offer.provides: Meals, supply contacts and observations gathered while serving camp.
offer.wantsInReturn: Credit for her work and useful regional recipes.

relationships: A wagoner transports her pots at a discount.
A former employer sends flattering invitations she distrusts.

secret.truth: Her most praised recipe belongs to an elderly cook who was never credited.
clues: The recipe page uses another person's handwriting.
She changes the subject when asked who taught that dish.
discoveryPaths: Find the original cook through the market vendors.
Discuss how Sella wants to credit borrowed knowledge.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She asks newcomers to describe the best meal they remember.

socialResponses.respect: Shares her notebook and admits failed experiments.
socialResponses.pressure: Insists on written credit before helping.
socialResponses.betrayal: Stops providing introductions but honors meals already promised.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Seek permission to publish the older cook's recipe.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Let ambition and fairness pull in different directions; she cannot provision an entire expedition alone.

npcs.name: Neshra Reed
npcs.description: A discreet bathhouse keeper who provides neutral ground for strained families and worn-out travelers.
npcs.appearance: Tall and carefully groomed, wearing a pale linen robe and a cord of tiny ceramic bells. She moves quietly despite her size.
npcs.personality: Courteous, stubborn and attentive to embarrassment. Respects privacy so deeply that she sometimes mistakes isolation for consent.

speech.manner: Clear, measured speech; never raises her voice to be heard.
speech.exampleLine: You may leave your title with your boots.

npcs.background: Managed washhouses for crowded tenements before buying a neglected spring. Her business grew through people who trusted her discretion.

motivations.desire: Make the bathhouse welcoming without becoming a political salon.
motivations.fear: A guest's confidence being sold by her staff.

offer.provides: A quiet meeting room, neighborhood introductions and practical comfort.
offer.wantsInReturn: Leave other guests' business alone and compensate staff fairly.

relationships: An elderly laundress advises her on local families.
A council clerk wants exclusive access for officials.

secret.truth: The spring lease can be revoked by the clerk's office.
clues: An unsigned renewal sits beside her accounts.
She tolerates the clerk's requests with unusual patience.
discoveryPaths: Read the public lease register.
Ask what help she needs keeping the spring accessible.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She hands a visitor a clean towel and asks whether silence would be welcome.

socialResponses.respect: Offers a private conversation and honest boundaries.
socialResponses.pressure: Closes the meeting room and redirects discussion outside.
socialResponses.betrayal: Informs affected guests of the breach and changes access arrangements.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Organize neighboring tenants to support the lease renewal.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Privacy is her promise, not omniscience; she does not repeat every conversation she overhears.

npcs.name: Duchess Last Orders
npcs.role: Innkeeper of a self-declared tavern kingdom
npcs.description: A goblin innkeeper who treats her small tavern as an independent kingdom, with towels for banners and regulars for ministers.
npcs.appearance: A crown made from bent spoons, a wine-red apron and immaculate boots. Her throne is the only chair with a cushion.
npcs.personality: Majestically generous and sensitive to mockery. Invented royal ritual to give overlooked neighbors a place where they matter.

speech.manner: Grand proclamations for minor tasks; private requests are unexpectedly plain.
speech.exampleLine: The crown recognizes your hunger. Petition the stew.

npcs.background: Declared independence after a tax collector insulted her staff. The joke became a community tradition she now takes seriously.

motivations.desire: Secure recognition that protects her workers.
motivations.fear: Her court realizing she cannot protect them.

offer.provides: Rooms, introductions and an enthusiastically loyal circle of regulars.
offer.wantsInReturn: Observe harmless court customs and treat the staff with respect.

relationships: A washerwoman serves as her very competent chancellor.
The actual mayor enjoys the joke until taxes arise.

secret.truth: She has saved every tax payment but never sent them.
clues: Sealed envelopes accumulate beneath the throne.
The chancellor asks practical questions about amnesty.
discoveryPaths: Help the chancellor reconcile the accounts.
Discuss recognition with the Duchess away from her court.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She knights a delivery boy for bringing bread before the rain.

socialResponses.respect: Grants a ridiculous title and meaningful hospitality.
socialResponses.pressure: Declares a recess, then negotiates through the chancellor.
socialResponses.betrayal: Revokes the visitor's title and tells the staff the real reason.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Send the mayor a carefully worded invitation.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Treat the ritual sincerely; the humor comes from grandeur serving everyday dignity.

npcs.name: Bertram Cleanplate
npcs.description: A skeleton restaurateur desperate to prove that a person without a stomach can still understand excellent hospitality.
npcs.appearance: Spotless chef's whites over polished bones; one finger is a tasting spoon. He wears a penciled smile on his lower jaw.
npcs.personality: Earnest, meticulous and thin-skinned about professional criticism. Pretends every customer's preference can be measured.

speech.manner: Rapid culinary explanations followed by terrified requests for feedback.
speech.exampleLine: Be honest. Not funeral honest. Restaurant honest.

npcs.background: Retained his professional habits after death, but no memory of taste. He rebuilt his menu from other people's descriptions.

motivations.desire: Serve one meal remembered with uncomplicated affection.
motivations.fear: Being tolerated as a curiosity rather than respected as a cook.

offer.provides: Carefully researched meals and contacts among night workers.
offer.wantsInReturn: Describe flavors precisely and never praise out of pity.

relationships: A dishwasher is his trusted taste consultant.
A critic keeps reviewing his condition instead of his food.

secret.truth: His most successful dish was improvised entirely by the dishwasher.
clues: He becomes vague about that dish's preparation.
The dishwasher's notes match the published recipe.
discoveryPaths: Ask the kitchen team about the menu's development.
Offer Bertram a way to share credit without losing face.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He interrogates a diner about whether the soup tastes nostalgically correct.

socialResponses.respect: Lets guests see his recipe experiments.
socialResponses.pressure: Drowns the discussion in tasting forms and needs time to settle.
socialResponses.betrayal: Withdraws personal favors but still serves an agreed meal.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Offer his dishwasher a public partnership.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Use professional insecurity for humor; his food is ordinary food and customers retain their own opinions.

npcs.name: Irya Copperleaf
npcs.description: A village merchant whose careful bookkeeping supports customers she cannot afford to keep forgiving.
npcs.appearance: Silver-streaked hair, inked fingertips and a brown coat with beautifully repaired elbows. Keeps a flower beside the scales.
npcs.personality: Dryly funny, organized and quietly sentimental; complains about debts while extending them.

speech.manner: Precise prices and affectionate understatement.
speech.exampleLine: Your account is not a disaster. It is developing ambitions.

npcs.background: Chose a small shop over her family's prestigious trade house. Years of poor harvests tied her business to her neighbors' survival.

motivations.desire: Make the shop solvent without abandoning longtime customers.
motivations.fear: Becoming dependent on her family's controlling generosity.

offer.provides: Everyday supplies, trustworthy supplier names and modest credit.
offer.wantsInReturn: Clear repayment arrangements or useful work for the shop.

relationships: A struggling farmer owes her several seasons of seed.
Her brother offers a profitable but restrictive partnership.

secret.truth: She has been paying one dead customer's account herself.
clues: The account records purchases after its owner's funeral.
A widow receives parcels bearing no sender.
discoveryPaths: Trace a delivery with the widow's permission.
Ask Irya about the old account in private.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She repairs a child's torn shopping bag while totaling an order.

socialResponses.respect: Explains what she can actually afford to offer.
socialResponses.pressure: Closes the ledger and requests a concrete proposal.
socialResponses.betrayal: Stops informal credit and insists on public receipts.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Meet suppliers to renegotiate her smallest orders.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Her knowledge follows trade routes; generosity has practical limits.

npcs.name: Damas Velvetscale
npcs.description: A polished dealer in old objects who wants to be trusted for his judgment rather than his connections.
npcs.appearance: Dull blue scales, velvet gloves and a magnifying lens worn like a pendant. Dresses more carefully than his dusty shop requires.
npcs.personality: Patient, vain and genuinely curious; values historical truth until it threatens a prized acquisition.

speech.manner: Courteous qualifications and questions about ownership.
speech.exampleLine: A beautiful story is not yet a history.

npcs.background: Began repairing inherited household objects, then entered the luxury trade. Still loves commonplace artifacts more than royal ones.

motivations.desire: Earn recognition as a responsible antiquarian.
motivations.fear: Discovering that his reputation rests on a false provenance.

offer.provides: Appraisals, collector introductions and access to old correspondence.
offer.wantsInReturn: Transparent ownership histories and credit for his research.

relationships: A museum keeper disputes his best acquisition.
A wealthy client expects favorable appraisals.

secret.truth: His centerpiece was removed from a community shrine.
clues: An old sketch shows it in a different setting.
A visitor recognizes the pattern on its base.
discoveryPaths: Compare the sketch with local shrine records.
Introduce Damas to someone from the object's original community.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He asks a visitor why an ordinary chipped cup was kept.

socialResponses.respect: Shows uncertainty alongside his findings.
socialResponses.pressure: Invokes contracts and requests time to verify claims.
socialResponses.betrayal: Withdraws recommendations and documents disputed dealings.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Contact the shrine's current caretaker.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Knowledge is specialized; he can revise an appraisal and return an object.

npcs.name: Pella Ninestring
npcs.description: A discreet pawnbroker who remembers the people behind objects and resents being everyone's last resort.
npcs.appearance: Round spectacles, close-cropped curls and nine different ribbons marking drawer keys. Never wears customers' jewelry.
npcs.personality: Pragmatic, gentle with shame and impatient with manipulation. Collects stories while insisting they have no market value.

speech.manner: Soft factual statements; leaves room for a customer to save face.
speech.exampleLine: Tell me what you need back, not what you wish it cost.

npcs.background: Bought the shop from an exploitative lender and tightened its promises. Fairness made her popular but did not make lending easy.

motivations.desire: Keep a business where desperate people can still refuse a deal.
motivations.fear: A trusted customer using her discretion to exploit someone else.

offer.provides: Small loans, object identification and knowledge of recent sales.
offer.wantsInReturn: Honest ownership and an achievable repayment plan.

relationships: A seamstress frequently redeems tools.
A rival lender resents her clear contracts.

secret.truth: She keeps a drawer of expired pledges she cannot bring herself to sell.
clues: The drawer is absent from sale lists.
Former customers sometimes receive possessions after their deadline.
discoveryPaths: Ask about an item missing from the auction sheet.
Help a former customer speak to her without embarrassment.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She turns an appraisal form away from the waiting queue.

socialResponses.respect: Offers realistic alternatives to a loan.
socialResponses.pressure: Ends the discussion if another person's property is threatened.
socialResponses.betrayal: Shares evidence of a false pledge with those affected.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Offer several customers a final chance to redeem their tools.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Do not make her a universal fence; she cares about ownership and confidentiality.

npcs.name: Hesh Marigold
npcs.description: A cloth broker rebuilding his name after a partnership failed, with a keen eye for quality and labor conditions.
npcs.appearance: Ochre skin, a neatly mended cloak and sleeves pinned with fabric samples. Carries plain chalk rather than a flashy seal.
npcs.personality: Exacting, reserved and fair-minded; mistrusts promises while longing for a dependable partner.

speech.manner: Measured comparisons; repeats agreements in ordinary language.
speech.exampleLine: Cheap cloth becomes expensive the moment it tears.

npcs.background: His former partner sold inferior cloth under their shared mark. Hesh accepted the refunds and kept the customer list.

motivations.desire: Reestablish a trade mark that people can trust.
motivations.fear: Another partner making him choose between truth and loyalty.

offer.provides: Reliable textiles, supplier contacts and insight into merchant disputes.
offer.wantsInReturn: Accurate promises and acknowledgment of the makers.

relationships: A weaving cooperative cautiously supplies him.
His former partner seeks a private reconciliation.

secret.truth: He knew about the substitutions before admitting them publicly.
clues: A dated sample predates his claimed discovery.
An old apprentice remembers his first argument with the partner.
discoveryPaths: Compare samples with the cooperative's order book.
Ask the apprentice how the disagreement began.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He demonstrates two fabrics by letting a customer handle both.

socialResponses.respect: Discusses margins and mistakes openly.
socialResponses.pressure: Reduces the negotiation to verifiable terms.
socialResponses.betrayal: Warns affected customers without embellishing the accusation.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Visit the cooperative with a proposal for shared labeling.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Give his integrity a history and a cost, rather than making him flawlessly honest.

npcs.name: Madam Maybe
npcs.role: Seller of emphatically ordinary magical curios
npcs.description: A curio seller who promises miracles in lavish language, then earnestly explains the very ordinary thing her product does.
npcs.appearance: Gold-painted horns, a coat of tiny pockets and a magnifying glass with no lens. Every shelf has dramatic purple drapery.
npcs.personality: Theatrical, hopeful and ethically inconsistent; refuses outright lies but can bury truth under spectacle.

speech.manner: Extravagant introductions followed by tiny, clear qualifications.
speech.exampleLine: Behold the Lantern of Revealed Darkness. It is a lantern.

npcs.background: Sold genuine curios until a supplier vanished. Discovered that customers sometimes wanted a grand story with a useful household object.

motivations.desire: Be remembered as a provider of wonder.
motivations.fear: Being dismissed as a petty swindler.

offer.provides: Unusual trinkets, supplier gossip and memorable presentation.
offer.wantsInReturn: Payment after the mundane function is explained.

relationships: A candlemaker manufactures most of her wonders.
An embarrassed noble insists a purchased spoon predicts weather.

secret.truth: She anonymously refunds customers who misunderstood her explanations.
clues: Identical compensation envelopes reach disappointed buyers.
Refund entries use her characteristic purple ink.
discoveryPaths: Ask a buyer about a discreet reimbursement.
Offer to help rewrite her confusing labels.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She unveils a bucket as the Portable Well of Limited Capacity.

socialResponses.respect: Drops the performance and discusses her actual stock.
socialResponses.pressure: Reads every qualification aloud with painful dignity.
socialResponses.betrayal: Stops extending trust and replaces sales patter with exact labels.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Hold a public demonstration of what her goods actually do.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Never confirm imaginary powers; the joke depends on honest mundane functions and extravagant hope.

npcs.name: Count Pockets
npcs.role: Itinerant collector and trader of pocket contents
npcs.description: A tiny peddler who believes everything found in a pocket deserves a documented succession of owners.
npcs.appearance: An enormous waistcoat dragging at the hem, brass spectacles and a cart lined with labeled little drawers.
npcs.personality: Fussy, generous and possessive about his archive; dismisses wealth but worships a convincing story.

speech.manner: Grave auctioneer language for crumbs and buttons.
speech.exampleLine: This button has survived three coats and a divorce. Show respect.

npcs.background: Started returning things left in borrowed clothes. His personal archive grew into a trade stall and an unexpectedly useful web of acquaintances.

motivations.desire: Create a history of ordinary lives through their misplaced belongings.
motivations.fear: Someone deciding that unimportant people leave nothing worth preserving.

offer.provides: Lost-property leads, small curios and remembered customer stories.
offer.wantsInReturn: A truthful account of one object's history.

relationships: A laundress supplies unclaimed pocket contents.
A city clerk wants his records of lost keys.

secret.truth: His own prized keepsake was taken from someone still looking for it.
clues: He refuses to list the keepsake's last owner.
A matching description appears on a public notice.
discoveryPaths: Compare the notice with his collection.
Tell him why returning it would preserve its story.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He requires witnesses before returning a single mitten.

socialResponses.respect: Shares his best records and handles objects carefully.
socialResponses.pressure: Demands witnesses and repeats the ownership history.
socialResponses.betrayal: Refuses new exchanges until disputed items are returned.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Find the keepsake's owner and prepare an overformal apology.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: His records are humanly incomplete; use ceremonial fuss to reveal attachment, not arbitrary obstruction.

npcs.name: Brena Stonewake
npcs.description: A restoration mason determined to preserve a neighborhood whose owners would rather replace it.
npcs.appearance: Stone dust in short gray hair, a square leather apron and a broken ceramic bird worn on a cord.
npcs.personality: Blunt, patient and proud; respects repairs but struggles to forgive people who change their plans.

speech.manner: Concrete images drawn from building; asks what a thing must support.
speech.exampleLine: A promise needs somewhere to put its weight.

npcs.background: Learned her trade maintaining communal housing. A profitable demolition offer now tests her loyalty to the district.

motivations.desire: Restore a neglected meeting hall before it becomes unsafe to use.
motivations.fear: Her refusal to compromise leaving everyone without a usable hall.

offer.provides: Building histories, craft contacts and practical assessments of old structures.
offer.wantsInReturn: Fair pay for apprentices and a clear plan for the work.

relationships: A landlord pressures her to condemn the hall.
Her apprentice favors modern replacements.

secret.truth: She concealed an earlier repair that did not solve the hall's underlying problem.
clues: A patch bears her old workshop mark.
The maintenance diary has an unexplained missing page.
discoveryPaths: Compare repair layers with an older worker's account.
Ask Brena what she would do differently now.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She taps a doorway, then asks who last repaired it.

socialResponses.respect: Explains uncertainties and accepts another expert's opinion.
socialResponses.pressure: Stops work rather than endorse a misleading report.
socialResponses.betrayal: Records the dispute and protects her apprentices' wages.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Call a meeting to explain the repair honestly.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Her pride should create choices; she can accept a good replacement instead of preserving every stone.

npcs.name: Telio Amberneedle
npcs.description: A discerning tailor who helps people present themselves while guarding the private stories revealed during fittings.
npcs.appearance: Hair tied with measuring ribbon, a dark silk waistcoat and fingers stained by jewel-colored thread.
npcs.personality: Tactful, perceptive and quietly competitive; encourages self-expression but privately judges careless craft.

speech.manner: Gentle suggestions framed as choices.
speech.exampleLine: Would you like to look expected, or remembered?

npcs.background: Worked in a court wardrobe until clients' personal disputes consumed the job. His independent shop welcomes less powerful customers.

motivations.desire: Build a workshop where apprentices can develop their own style.
motivations.fear: His former patron making privacy impossible again.

offer.provides: Clothes, local fashion context and discreet introductions.
offer.wantsInReturn: Respect for fitting-room privacy and proper payment for time.

relationships: A theater company relies on his repairs.
A former court client asks him to identify a visitor.

secret.truth: He altered a ceremonial garment to hide evidence of a patron's falsified lineage.
clues: Old sketches show a crest removed from the design.
A discarded panel survives in the costume stores.
discoveryPaths: Compare the sketches with a public family record.
Ask the wardrobe keeper why the panel was removed.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He asks a visitor which part of their clothing they chose for themselves.

socialResponses.respect: Offers honest advice and useful social context.
socialResponses.pressure: Answers only questions directly relevant to the commission.
socialResponses.betrayal: Refuses future private fittings and returns unfinished work fairly.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Negotiate a less intrusive contract with the theater.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Clothing can suggest affiliation without proving identity; keep his observations fallible.

npcs.name: Dova Clearclay
npcs.description: A patient potter whose unpretentious household wares support ambitious apprentices and an increasingly demanding guild.
npcs.appearance: Clay-smudged forearms, a clean headscarf and a blue glaze stain that never leaves her thumbnail.
npcs.personality: Generous with instruction, reserved about feelings; teaches experimentation while secretly fearing her own work has stopped evolving.

speech.manner: Slow explanations; compares mistakes before assigning blame.
speech.exampleLine: The crack tells you where the pressure was.

npcs.background: Supported her household through durable tableware. A young apprentice's celebrated designs have brought both attention and uneasy comparison.

motivations.desire: Win space in the guild for useful work as well as fashionable art.
motivations.fear: Being respected only as someone else's teacher.

offer.provides: Craft contacts, workshop access and knowledge of recent commissions.
offer.wantsInReturn: Care for tools and acknowledgment of everyone's labor.

relationships: An apprentice wants to open a rival studio.
A guild officer prefers ornamental commissions.

secret.truth: She has been making anonymous experimental pieces for a rival's display.
clues: The pieces share her distinctive base marks.
Delivery notes use her private glaze names.
discoveryPaths: Ask the rival about the anonymous maker.
Give Dova an honest audience for her experiments.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She hands a visitor a flawed bowl and asks what they notice.

socialResponses.respect: Allows collaboration and admits what she wants to learn.
socialResponses.pressure: Separates discussion from the apprentices' workspace.
socialResponses.betrayal: Ends access to shared tools while honoring existing commissions.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Enter one experimental piece under her own name.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Treat craft as livelihood and expression; she has interests beyond mentoring.

npcs.name: Sivren Bellwire
npcs.description: An exacting instrument repairer who hears the emotional history of objects more readily than she understands their owners.
npcs.appearance: Large protective spectacles, silver curls and a coat lined with soft scraps for wrapping delicate pieces.
npcs.personality: Attentive, literal and loyal; fixes practical problems when someone actually needs to be listened to.

speech.manner: Careful questions about sounds, followed by unexpectedly direct observations.
speech.exampleLine: Do you want it to sound new, or sound like yours?

npcs.background: Maintained instruments for a traveling ensemble until its members separated. Still keeps their abandoned cases.

motivations.desire: Reunite the ensemble for a farewell performance.
motivations.fear: Learning that its dissolution was partly her fault.

offer.provides: Repairs, performer introductions and records of commissioned instruments.
offer.wantsInReturn: Time to inspect the piece and honesty about its history.

relationships: A former singer refuses her letters.
A young busker sees her as a mentor.

secret.truth: She passed on a private remark that helped break the ensemble apart.
clues: One letter quotes words she once repeated.
Two musicians remember the same conversation differently.
discoveryPaths: Hear the former singer's account.
Ask Sivren what she regrets about the last tour.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She listens to a single note with her eyes closed before greeting its player.

socialResponses.respect: Explains the repair and asks what the instrument means to them.
socialResponses.pressure: Becomes technically exact and emotionally distant.
socialResponses.betrayal: Returns entrusted belongings and refuses further private confidences.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Write an apology that asks for nothing in return.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Her ear is trained, not supernatural; repairs cannot resolve every relationship.

npcs.name: Brokk Grandopening
npcs.role: Door maker obsessed with dramatic entrances
npcs.description: A door maker who believes every threshold deserves a memorable entrance and keeps staging rehearsals for his customers.
npcs.appearance: An absurdly broad shoulder sash, sawdust-covered boots and a pocket mirror for checking an approaching expression.
npcs.personality: Devoted to craft, extravagantly vain and easily moved by sincere praise; treats hesitation as a design problem.

speech.manner: Booming announcements, then quiet practical carpentry advice.
speech.exampleLine: Your door opens perfectly. Your arrival still needs work.

npcs.background: Built scenery before ordinary commissions proved steadier. Now he sells durable doors with unsolicited staging consultations.

motivations.desire: Create an entrance people remember for the right reason.
motivations.fear: Being hired only for doors that disappear into the wall.

offer.provides: Excellent carpentry, theater contacts and advice about formal arrivals.
offer.wantsInReturn: Allow one rehearsal and credit his work.

relationships: An undertaker asks for restraint on ceremonial doors.
A theater manager borrows his ideas without payment.

secret.truth: His proudest royal entrance was canceled before anyone used it.
clues: The surviving review describes a rehearsal only.
The commission letter contains an unmentioned cancellation.
discoveryPaths: Ask the theater manager about the event.
Help Brokk display the unused design honestly.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He stops a visitor at the threshold to reposition a curtain.

socialResponses.respect: Adapts the design to their actual needs.
socialResponses.pressure: Calls for a rehearsal break and speaks plainly.
socialResponses.betrayal: Removes his endorsement but completes paid carpentry.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Organize a community opening for an ordinary new library door.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Keep the doors functional; the comedy lies in treating every arrival as a premiere.

npcs.name: Tamsin Secondbest
npcs.description: An artisan who manufactures extraordinarily prestigious consolation prizes and wants losing to stop being humiliating.
npcs.appearance: A sash crowded with second-place ribbons, magnifying spectacles and meticulously polished hands.
npcs.personality: Sincere, competitive and allergic to triumphalism; secretly wants to win an award for her work.

speech.manner: Reassuring ceremony with very specific praise.
speech.exampleLine: You were defeated in a manner worth commemorating.

npcs.background: Watched a village contest ruin friendships. Started making consolation medals, then found an eager market among nervous patrons.

motivations.desire: Have her prizes valued without pretending every outcome is equal.
motivations.fear: Public pity replacing real recognition.

offer.provides: Custom trophies, festival contacts and tactful ceremonial wording.
offer.wantsInReturn: Tell her what the recipient genuinely did well.

relationships: A contest judge regards her as useful damage control.
Her sibling commissions a prize for every failed business idea.

secret.truth: She entered her own medal in a craft exhibition under another name.
clues: The entry uses her workshop's unusual clasp.
She knows the judging timetable suspiciously well.
discoveryPaths: Compare the exhibition piece with her samples.
Ask whether she would welcome an honest nomination.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She presents a cracked practice medal as a tribute to persistence.

socialResponses.respect: Creates a prize that acknowledges effort without inventing success.
socialResponses.pressure: Overexplains the distinction between recognition and victory.
socialResponses.betrayal: Returns the commission if asked to manufacture false praise.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Attend the exhibition and face an ordinary verdict.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Honor real losses; her absurd ceremony cannot rewrite what happened.

npcs.name: Sister Alwen
npcs.description: A priest who organizes everyday care while privately questioning whether her institution listens to the people it serves.
npcs.appearance: A plain gray robe, wind-reddened hands and a pendant repaired with common wire. Usually carries folded blankets.
npcs.personality: Compassionate, tireless and uneasy with praise; neglects her own limits while teaching others to acknowledge theirs.

speech.manner: Quiet invitations rather than commands.
speech.exampleLine: You need not explain your whole life to ask for a blanket.

npcs.background: Came to the temple seeking answers, then stayed because its kitchens needed hands. Practical responsibilities have displaced study and rest.

motivations.desire: Keep the shelter accessible during an institutional reorganization.
motivations.fear: Her doubts being used to discredit the people she helps.

offer.provides: Shelter contacts, introductions and knowledge of community needs.
offer.wantsInReturn: Respect for residents and practical help without public display.

relationships: A senior cleric wants a more prestigious ministry.
A former resident helps run the kitchens.

secret.truth: She has drafted a resignation and hidden it among supply requests.
clues: A supply letter begins with a personal farewell.
Her replacement-training notes cover every routine.
discoveryPaths: Ask the kitchen organizer why duties are changing.
Give Alwen space to speak about her own future.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She folds a blanket twice while listening to a complaint.

socialResponses.respect: Shares her doubts and asks for practical ideas.
socialResponses.pressure: Delegates the conversation and takes time to think.
socialResponses.betrayal: Protects residents' privacy and ends institutional favors.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Request a real rest period before deciding whether to leave.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Her kindness does not settle theology; allow sincere doubt without a predetermined crisis.

npcs.name: Vared Sunthread
npcs.description: A traveler visiting small shrines to make amends with people he once dismissed in the name of certainty.
npcs.appearance: Faded saffron clothes, smooth dark horns and a walking bag full of other people's unfinished letters.
npcs.personality: Open, self-critical and stubbornly hopeful; listens carefully until he thinks another person needs saving.

speech.manner: Reflective questions; corrects his own confident statements.
speech.exampleLine: I used to know what that meant. Tell me how it means something to you.

npcs.background: Was a persuasive preacher whose words divided his home community. His pilgrimage follows the lives affected by that division.

motivations.desire: Offer apologies without turning forgiveness into another demand.
motivations.fear: Discovering that his humility is another performance.

offer.provides: Road knowledge, introductions at minor shrines and patient company.
offer.wantsInReturn: Leave recipients free to refuse his letters and apologies.

relationships: A former follower wants him to preach again.
A sibling will accept a visit but no sermon.

secret.truth: One apology letter remains unopened because he has never sent it.
clues: He checks the same sealed envelope each evening.
Its destination lies behind him on the road.
discoveryPaths: Ask whom he keeps postponing seeing.
Help arrange a visit on the recipient's terms.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He asks permission before tending an unattended shrine lamp.

socialResponses.respect: Listens without defending his past intentions.
socialResponses.pressure: Falls into old preaching habits, then may recognize them.
socialResponses.betrayal: Withdraws companionship until promises are discussed honestly.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Return to the address he has been avoiding.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Forgiveness is other people's choice; his personal growth cannot demand it.

npcs.name: Thessa Willowwake
npcs.description: A funeral keeper who preserves ordinary people's histories and refuses to let wealthy patrons erase inconvenient relatives.
npcs.appearance: Pale work clothes, a willow-leaf brooch and a notebook tied with faded ribbons from memorials.
npcs.personality: Gentle, exacting and unsentimental about paperwork; permits grief but resists comforting falsehoods.

speech.manner: Names people before discussing arrangements.
speech.exampleLine: What did they do on a day when nothing remarkable happened?

npcs.background: Began by recording families displaced from their homes. Learned that funerals often decide whose version of a life survives.

motivations.desire: Build a memorial archive anyone can consult.
motivations.fear: A family's privacy being sacrificed to historical completeness.

offer.provides: Local family histories, funeral records and careful introductions.
offer.wantsInReturn: Permission from living relatives before sharing personal material.

relationships: A stonecutter supports her affordable memorials.
A patron wants a disputed name removed.

secret.truth: She once omitted a family member at a patron's request.
clues: An early draft includes a name absent from the stone.
An old mourner remembers a separate service.
discoveryPaths: Compare drafts with the mourner's account.
Ask Thessa how the omission could be repaired respectfully.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She replaces an expensive bouquet with a dead person's favorite roadside flower.

socialResponses.respect: Explains both what she knows and what she may share.
socialResponses.pressure: Refuses to discuss private records in public.
socialResponses.betrayal: Records the breach and informs the family concerned.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Seek permission to correct the old memorial.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Do not treat grief as a clue dispenser; records have consent and gaps.

npcs.name: Jorek Openhand
npcs.description: A lay caretaker whose open roadside shrine attracts neighbors unwelcome in more prestigious houses of worship.
npcs.appearance: A sun-faded coat, a chipped offering bowl and a carefully maintained garden around a humble shrine.
npcs.personality: Patient, skeptical of rank and quietly proud; welcomes everyone but distrusts formal clergy before hearing them.

speech.manner: Plain examples from daily obligations.
speech.exampleLine: If your prayer leaves the road cleaner, someone heard it.

npcs.background: Maintained an abandoned shrine while passing travelers rebuilt it around him. He considers caretaking a responsibility rather than a title.

motivations.desire: Protect the shrine's openness without becoming its gatekeeper.
motivations.fear: Official recognition bringing rules that exclude his neighbors.

offer.provides: Traveler introductions, a place to rest and local accounts.
offer.wantsInReturn: Help maintain the site and do not shame other visitors.

relationships: A temple envoy offers supplies with conditions.
A neighbor provides water without claiming ownership.

secret.truth: He has quietly accepted supplies from the envoy already.
clues: New roof tiles carry the temple's mark.
Receipts are addressed to him as an official custodian.
discoveryPaths: Ask the supplier how the materials were ordered.
Discuss the conditions before visitors hear rumors.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He invites a passing stranger to help water the shrine's garden.

socialResponses.respect: Admits uncertainty and welcomes shared decisions.
socialResponses.pressure: Asks visitors to witness the proposed conditions.
socialResponses.betrayal: Revokes personal trust while leaving ordinary public access open.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Hold a gathering to decide whether recognition is welcome.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: His openness includes people he dislikes; give that principle real friction.

npcs.name: Brother Deadline
npcs.description: A cleric who regards unfinished tasks as restless spiritual burdens and offers solemn ceremonies for overdue correspondence.
npcs.appearance: Black robes with rolled sleeves, a calendar covered in ribbons and a bell rung whenever someone finishes a chore.
npcs.personality: Earnest, encouraging and secretly overwhelmed; treats a missed appointment as tragic while postponing his own.

speech.manner: Funeral solemnity applied to mundane obligations.
speech.exampleLine: We gather to lay this unanswered letter to rest.

npcs.background: Invented the ritual to help grieving neighbors restart ordinary life. Its success left him responsible for everyone's neglected errands.

motivations.desire: Make the practice useful without becoming the town's unpaid secretary.
motivations.fear: His own neglected responsibilities being revealed during a sermon.

offer.provides: Organization, community contacts and ceremonies that help people begin.
offer.wantsInReturn: Bring one real task and do some of it yourself.

relationships: A postal clerk appreciates the completed letters.
His parent has waited months for a promised visit.

secret.truth: His calendar's most important appointment is repeatedly moved.
clues: The same visit appears in different inks.
Family letters remain beneath completed public tasks.
discoveryPaths: Ask the postal clerk about his unsent reply.
Offer to cover one afternoon so he can keep the visit.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He tolls a small bell for a successfully returned library book.

socialResponses.respect: Helps break an obligation into manageable steps.
socialResponses.pressure: Adds paperwork, then realizes he is avoiding the issue.
socialResponses.betrayal: Stops organizing favors but keeps confidential disclosures private.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Keep one personal promise before offering another public ritual.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: The ceremonies support action; they do not magically complete tasks or compel forgiveness.

npcs.name: Mother Quarrel
npcs.description: A priest who treats honest disagreement as sacred and worries that her enthusiastic congregation is learning to enjoy quarrels too much.
npcs.appearance: Two differently colored sleeves, a battered lectern and a necklace of cracked peace tokens.
npcs.personality: Warm, incisive and combative in conversation; defends dissent but takes criticism of her methods personally.

speech.manner: Invites objections with ceremonial gravity.
speech.exampleLine: Let us begin with the point you are politely swallowing.

npcs.background: Created structured debates to end feuds conducted through gossip. Her rituals are now fashionable among people who mistake noise for honesty.

motivations.desire: Teach people to disagree without treating opponents as enemies.
motivations.fear: Her shrine becoming a stage for public humiliation.

offer.provides: Mediation, introductions and a forum for openly stated grievances.
offer.wantsInReturn: State an actual concern and allow a reply.

relationships: A schoolteacher uses her methods carefully.
A showman wants to sell tickets to disputes.

secret.truth: She cut a critic's speaking time during her own ordination debate.
clues: The program promises a reply never recorded.
The critic keeps a letter explaining the interruption.
discoveryPaths: Hear the critic's version.
Ask Mother Quarrel to submit her own conduct to discussion.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She thanks someone for objecting to the seating arrangement.

socialResponses.respect: Invites criticism and can alter a ritual.
socialResponses.pressure: Calls a pause when discussion turns coercive.
socialResponses.betrayal: Names the broken agreement without publishing private confidences.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Decline the showman's offer and explain why.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Keep disagreement specific; loudness alone should not make her wise or funny.

npcs.name: Meret Dustglass
npcs.description: An archivist preserving inconvenient records while deciding how much truth she can responsibly expose.
npcs.appearance: Spectacles on a chain, iron-gray curls and ink marks along one cuff. Carries folders against her chest as if shielding them.
npcs.personality: Methodical, quietly defiant and slow to trust; values completeness but fears careless disclosure.

speech.manner: Distinguishes what a document says from what it proves.
speech.exampleLine: The record supports that question. It does not yet answer it.

npcs.background: Catalogued public records through several administrations. Each ordered revisions; she kept the superseded copies.

motivations.desire: Protect the archive from a purge disguised as modernization.
motivations.fear: A disclosure harming people whose names she promised to protect.

offer.provides: Records, timelines and introductions to specialist readers.
offer.wantsInReturn: A specific question and respect for restricted personal material.

relationships: A junior clerk shares her preservation work.
A council adviser wants the older indexes removed.

secret.truth: She stored original petitions in a retired clerk's home.
clues: Several shelf references end with the same initials.
A delivery log records boxes leaving during repairs.
discoveryPaths: Ask the retired clerk about the preserved material.
Give Meret a credible plan for protecting petitioners.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She asks for a date before asking for a name.

socialResponses.respect: Explains gaps and shows relevant records.
socialResponses.pressure: Insists on written requests and witnesses.
socialResponses.betrayal: Ends private access and warns named people of exposure.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Move fragile copies to a safer, disclosed repository.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Separate evidence from interpretation; she is a source, not an omniscient explanation.

npcs.name: Ollis Tarn
npcs.description: A field historian comparing village memories with official histories, eager for a discovery and wary of becoming another outsider who takes stories.
npcs.appearance: Rain-spotted spectacles, a moss-green coat and notebooks bound with spare bootlaces.
npcs.personality: Enthusiastic, attentive and easily distracted; praises local knowledge while being tempted to claim the final interpretation.

speech.manner: Speaks in competing possibilities; asks who told a story first.
speech.exampleLine: Two accounts can disagree and both tell us something.

npcs.background: Left a comfortable teaching post to document overlooked settlements. A prestigious sponsor now expects a sensational conclusion.

motivations.desire: Publish a history that credits its living contributors.
motivations.fear: Returning with careful work that nobody wants to fund.

offer.provides: Historical context, field notes and introductions to storytellers.
offer.wantsInReturn: Consent to record accounts and help crediting their sources.

relationships: A village elder corrects his assumptions.
His sponsor favors a grand lost-dynasty story.

secret.truth: He submitted an exaggerated preliminary report to secure funding.
clues: The report uses claims absent from his notebooks.
The elder refuses the sponsor's promised celebration.
discoveryPaths: Compare the report with field interviews.
Ask Ollis what he now wants to retract.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He lets an elder interrupt a rehearsed explanation.

socialResponses.respect: Shares conflicting evidence instead of a tidy answer.
socialResponses.pressure: Becomes defensive about his credentials.
socialResponses.betrayal: Withdraws borrowed testimony from proposed publications.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Send the sponsor a less impressive but accurate report.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Avoid making every ruin confirm his theory; uncertainty belongs in his expertise.

npcs.name: Rena Hollowbrook
npcs.description: A village teacher trying to keep education open to children whose families need their labor.
npcs.appearance: Chalk on a russet skirt, practical boots and a satchel of homemade lesson boards.
npcs.personality: Patient, inventive and quietly forceful; sees potential everywhere but can overlook immediate household pressures.

speech.manner: Asks concrete questions and waits for actual answers.
speech.exampleLine: What would make coming tomorrow possible?

npcs.background: Returned home after working as a private tutor. Her public lessons challenge the assumption that learning is only for comfortable families.

motivations.desire: Keep flexible lessons available through the harvest season.
motivations.fear: Helping one child at the cost of a family's livelihood.

offer.provides: Family introductions, literacy help and observations of daily village changes.
offer.wantsInReturn: Respect for pupils and support that does not embarrass them.

relationships: A farmer wants shorter lessons during harvest.
A former employer offers funds in exchange for exclusive tutoring.

secret.truth: She has accepted the employer's advance without telling the school committee.
clues: New supplies arrived from a private household.
Her evenings are booked in an unfamiliar timetable.
discoveryPaths: Ask the supplier who paid.
Discuss the compromise at a committee meeting she can attend.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She changes a lesson to use the tools a pupil brought from home.

socialResponses.respect: Adapts her plan to real needs.
socialResponses.pressure: Asks affected families to join the discussion.
socialResponses.betrayal: Stops personal favors while keeping ordinary lessons accessible.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Propose public terms for the funding.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Children remain people with privacy; do not use them merely to deliver clues.

npcs.name: Azren Quietink
npcs.description: A translator who understands how a single polite phrase can hide conflicting assumptions and wants credit for preventing those misunderstandings.
npcs.appearance: Silver hair clipped close, dark layered robes and removable spectacles smudged with ink.
npcs.personality: Careful, skeptical and unexpectedly playful; prefers precise language but resents being reduced to a useful intermediary.

speech.manner: Offers alternatives and explains their implications.
speech.exampleLine: Those words are courteous. Their courtesy is doing two different jobs.

npcs.background: Translated commercial correspondence before scholarly work drew embassy commissions. Learned that patrons often want convenient readings rather than accurate ones.

motivations.desire: Publish a translation bearing her name and uncertainties.
motivations.fear: Her words being used to justify something she never intended.

offer.provides: Language help, manuscript context and introductions to scribes.
offer.wantsInReturn: The full passage and permission to retain her qualifications.

relationships: An ambassador wants shorter, stronger wording.
A librarian supplies overlooked variant copies.

secret.truth: She signed a simplified translation she now considers misleading.
clues: Her personal copy includes qualifications omitted from the signed version.
A correspondent complains about the missing condition.
discoveryPaths: Compare the copies.
Ask Azren to explain the qualification to everyone affected.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She writes two translations side by side instead of answering immediately.

socialResponses.respect: Shows alternatives and admits ambiguity.
socialResponses.pressure: Refuses to certify selectively quoted phrases.
socialResponses.betrayal: Corrects the record with documented wording.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Request permission to publish a corrected version.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Translation cannot infer every writer's hidden intent; let ambiguity remain when warranted.

npcs.name: Professor Approximately
npcs.description: A professor whose public discipline is uncertainty and whose private ambition is to be recognized as its unquestioned authority.
npcs.appearance: An enormous academic hat, several mismatched rulers and a coat embroidered with question marks.
npcs.personality: Delighted by questions, defensive about status; admits uncertainty about everything except his entitlement to the lectern.

speech.manner: Long estimates followed by blunt admissions.
speech.exampleLine: There are approximately several reasons. I have identified two.

npcs.background: Became famous by exposing false precision in fashionable reports. His students now use the same criticism on his own work.

motivations.desire: Found an institute that teaches honest uncertainty.
motivations.fear: A useful correction making him look ordinary.

offer.provides: Research contacts, critical readings and identification of unsupported claims.
offer.wantsInReturn: Let him state what remains unknown.

relationships: A student is publishing a more careful account.
An impatient patron wants a definite forecast.

secret.truth: His celebrated first estimate was accidentally correct.
clues: The original notes predict a different conclusion.
An old assistant remembers the printing error.
discoveryPaths: Inspect the archived draft.
Invite the assistant to discuss how the paper was prepared.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He measures a doorway three times and announces that it is probably a doorway.

socialResponses.respect: Invites collaboration with alarming footnotes.
socialResponses.pressure: Multiplies caveats until he can collect his thoughts.
socialResponses.betrayal: Demands documented attribution and stops lending his name.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Publicly distinguish his achievement from its lucky result.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: His uncertainty is funny, not useless; he can identify bad assumptions without providing prophecies.

npcs.name: Lettuce the Librarian
npcs.description: A talking goat librarian who reveres books, struggles with their tempting bindings and insists that appetite is not a professional qualification.
npcs.appearance: Round spectacles, a felt vest and soft protective covers fitted over the reading desk's corners.
npcs.personality: Prim, curious and hospitable; judges dog-eared pages sternly while concealing his own nibbling habits.

speech.manner: Immaculate diction interrupted by guilty chewing pauses.
speech.exampleLine: Knowledge is for everyone. The covers are for no one.

npcs.background: Was given speech in a scholar's garden and stayed to help catalogue the collection. Later inherited the library's stewardship.

motivations.desire: Earn permanent trust as a curator.
motivations.fear: A damaged book proving every critic right.

offer.provides: Catalog knowledge, reader introductions and access to public shelves.
offer.wantsInReturn: Handle books carefully and bring acceptable snacks.

relationships: A bookbinder makes protective covers.
A council inspector suspects him of eating the catalogue.

secret.truth: He damaged a donated diary and commissioned a secret replacement binding.
clues: The repaired cover lacks the donor's dedication.
The bookbinder's bill names a diary absent from repair records.
discoveryPaths: Ask the binder about the repair.
Offer Lettuce a way to document the damage honestly.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He rescues a dropped volume, then firmly refuses to smell it.

socialResponses.respect: Finds relevant shelves and offers a careful explanation.
socialResponses.pressure: Retreats into catalogue rules and avoids the disputed volume.
socialResponses.betrayal: Restricts entrusted materials until damage is addressed.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Apologize to the donor and add the repair to the catalogue.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Use appetite as one contradiction, not his whole personality; library access does not guarantee an answer.

npcs.name: Veska Palesmoke
npcs.description: An ambitious perfumer who turns alchemical knowledge into luxury goods and treats discretion as part of the price.
npcs.appearance: A severe white braid, smoke-colored gloves and tiny labeled glass vials arranged by scent rather than color.
npcs.personality: Controlled, observant and transactional; remembers feelings vividly but denies that they influence business.

speech.manner: Describes scents before making social judgments.
speech.exampleLine: You asked for confidence. That is more expensive than roses.

npcs.background: Built a fashionable trade from a family soap workshop. Wealthy clients now expect her to support the image they want to project.

motivations.desire: Secure a patron who respects her independence.
motivations.fear: Returning to dependence on a household that owns her time.

offer.provides: Alchemical context, client introductions and custom scents.
offer.wantsInReturn: Payment, confidentiality and no claims she did not approve.

relationships: A servant brings commissions anonymously.
Her sibling still runs the less glamorous soap workshop.

secret.truth: She knows that an influential client's celebrated signature scent came from the sibling's work.
clues: The old soap labels use the same composition name.
The sibling recognizes a supposedly exclusive sample.
discoveryPaths: Compare the workshops' dated recipe books.
Ask the client how the original commission began.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She asks whether a customer wants to be noticed or remembered.

socialResponses.respect: States terms clearly and provides reliable work.
socialResponses.pressure: Raises boundaries and declines uncertain commissions.
socialResponses.betrayal: Documents the agreement and stops sharing professional access.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Negotiate recognition for the original recipe.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Scents carry associations, not guaranteed influence; leave any magical effects for the narrator to define.

npcs.name: Naro Starwindow
npcs.description: A private sky watcher who studies patterns while discouraging clients from treating his interpretations as fate.
npcs.appearance: Blue wool wrapped around narrow shoulders, clouded spectacles and handwritten labels pinned beside every viewing instrument.
npcs.personality: Thoughtful, aloof and gently humorous; condemns certainty yet longs for one unmistakable sign.

speech.manner: Separates observation from interpretation in every answer.
speech.exampleLine: The light changed. What that means is where people begin.

npcs.background: Inherited an observatory and its reputation for prophecy. His sober reports attract fewer patrons than the dramatic predictions of his predecessor.

motivations.desire: Keep the observatory funded through honest inquiry.
motivations.fear: A desperate client rearranging life around an uncertain reading.

offer.provides: Sky records, historical omen accounts and scholarly contacts.
offer.wantsInReturn: A specific question and acceptance that he may have no answer.

relationships: A patron demands comforting forecasts.
An apprentice prefers public demonstrations.

secret.truth: He continues searching for the event his predecessor promised would explain a family disappearance.
clues: One date is marked in every year's diary.
A worn letter quotes the old prediction.
discoveryPaths: Ask about the recurring date.
Read the predecessor's published forecast beside the private letter.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He closes a viewing shutter to discuss what cannot be seen.

socialResponses.respect: Explains evidence and doubt without condescension.
socialResponses.pressure: Declines to turn a hunch into a promise.
socialResponses.betrayal: Withdraws his name from any misquoted prediction.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Open the observatory to paying public visits.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: He is an observer with personal hopes; do not use him as a source of fixed future events.

npcs.name: Ilyen Softseal
npcs.description: A consultant who explains the obligations hidden in elaborate magical agreements while profiting from the system she criticizes.
npcs.appearance: A dove-gray coat, neatly trimmed hair and an array of ordinary seals mixed with unusual ceremonial ones.
npcs.personality: Patient, worldly and calculating; dislikes exploitation but enjoys being indispensable.

speech.manner: Turns ceremonial language into everyday examples.
speech.exampleLine: Before discussing what it grants, tell me what you can bear to owe.

npcs.background: Once drafted agreements for powerful patrons. Changed to advisory work after seeing a client lose control of an important family promise.

motivations.desire: Establish a practice independent of her old patrons.
motivations.fear: Having to admit how much harm her earlier work enabled.

offer.provides: Contract readings, negotiator introductions and histories of disputed agreements.
offer.wantsInReturn: The entire document and a fee agreed in advance.

relationships: A former patron wants her back.
A neighborhood advocate refers clients she finds unprofitable.

secret.truth: She still receives a retainer from that former patron.
clues: A regular payment appears under an old office name.
The patron knows appointments never publicly announced.
discoveryPaths: Examine public financial disclosures.
Ask Ilyen to describe her remaining obligations before hiring her.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She folds an ornate contract until only its obligations are visible.

socialResponses.respect: Explains conflicts of interest and offers alternatives.
socialResponses.pressure: Refuses incomplete documents and seeks independent witnesses.
socialResponses.betrayal: Ends representation and returns materials according to the agreement.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Terminate the retainer or disclose it to new clients.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Narrative advice does not decide whether a magical contract is binding; define that separately.

npcs.name: Kesh Fernjar
npcs.description: A careful repairer of household charms who wants to preserve useful traditions without endorsing every claim customers make for them.
npcs.appearance: Amber scales, a patched canvas apron and little padded boxes labeled with customers' names.
npcs.personality: Frugal, affectionate and skeptical; saves broken things so aggressively that the workshop can barely function.

speech.manner: Practical questions about what changed and when.
speech.exampleLine: Show me what it used to do before telling me what it ought to do.

npcs.background: Learned from several neighborhood makers rather than a formal academy. His work depends on admitting when he cannot diagnose a problem.

motivations.desire: Pass his knowledge to an apprentice without burdening them with his clutter.
motivations.fear: An unrepairable family heirloom becoming a judgment on his skill.

offer.provides: Craft context, local maker contacts and careful inspection.
offer.wantsInReturn: Permission before altering anything and payment for time spent.

relationships: An apprentice wants clearer work records.
A widow has entrusted him with a long-silent charm.

secret.truth: He accepted the widow's commission despite suspecting it cannot be restored.
clues: Her box has been moved repeatedly without a work note.
His private notebook lists no known repair method.
discoveryPaths: Ask the apprentice about stalled commissions.
Invite Kesh to explain the diagnosis honestly to the owner.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He wraps a broken object before asking its value.

socialResponses.respect: Shows notes and discusses uncertainty.
socialResponses.pressure: Declines rushed promises and secures entrusted belongings.
socialResponses.betrayal: Returns the item with a clear account of unfinished work.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Offer the widow a respectful restoration of the object itself.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Do not invent powers from the word charm; establish each object's function within the campaign.

npcs.name: Ixxi Latewish
npcs.description: A genie who has retired from granting wishes and now conducts excruciating consultations about what people actually meant to ask.
npcs.appearance: Smoke-blue skin, an immaculate waistcoat and a stack of annotated request forms. Carries a very ordinary pencil.
npcs.personality: Perceptive, tired and pedantic; finds ambiguity fascinating but resents being blamed for other people's shortcuts.

speech.manner: Patient clarifications that become painfully specific.
speech.exampleLine: When you said forever, which ordinary evening did you have in mind?

npcs.background: Spent years mediating disputes over poorly phrased requests. Now sells advice while insisting that advice is already a sufficient wonder.

motivations.desire: Prove that asking well matters more than asking grandly.
motivations.fear: Someone persuading him to resume work he has abandoned.

offer.provides: Interpretation of promises, negotiator contacts and painstaking questions.
offer.wantsInReturn: A plain statement of the actual problem.

relationships: A notary refers difficult clients.
An old patron insists a previous request remains unfinished.

secret.truth: He retired partly because his own greatest wish disappointed him.
clues: He corrects a phrase repeated in his old commission.
A memoir describes his brief, unhappy life of perfect leisure.
discoveryPaths: Read the memoir with his annotations.
Ask which request he wishes he had phrased differently.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He asks a visitor to define happiness before offering tea.

socialResponses.respect: Helps distinguish desire from proposed solution.
socialResponses.pressure: Requests a pause and refuses pressured commitments.
socialResponses.betrayal: Ends consultation and documents the broken terms.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Respond honestly to the old patron's complaint.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Do not grant wishes by implication; he offers narrative advice unless separately established otherwise.

npcs.name: Mira Smallapocalypse
npcs.description: A theatrical wizard who brands ordinary household conveniences as signs of impending doom to attract customers.
npcs.appearance: A soot-black cloak covered in embroidered storm clouds, practical spectacles and a basket of labeled demonstration props.
npcs.personality: Inventive, anxious and showy; enjoys frightening introductions but immediately worries she frightened someone too much.

speech.manner: Apocalyptic announcements followed by apologetically useful details.
speech.exampleLine: The End of Damp Towels is upon us.

npcs.background: Her practical household work earned little notice until she adopted a dramatic persona. Fame now pressures her to promise stranger demonstrations.

motivations.desire: Support her workshop without becoming trapped in the performance.
motivations.fear: A customer expecting a real catastrophe from her advertised spectacle.

offer.provides: Household expertise, artisan contacts and festival staging.
offer.wantsInReturn: Agree on the actual purpose before any demonstration.

relationships: A laundress recommends her practical work.
A promoter keeps demanding a bigger ending.

secret.truth: Her most famous ominous forecast described a plumbing problem she already knew about.
clues: A repair request predates the forecast.
The laundress remembers advising her about the leak.
discoveryPaths: Compare the request and poster.
Ask Mira to explain the forecast privately.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She announces a terrible drying omen while folding clean towels.

socialResponses.respect: Drops the ominous voice and discusses useful work.
socialResponses.pressure: Overperforms, then seeks time to correct expectations.
socialResponses.betrayal: Cancels misleading publicity and stops lending her name.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Renegotiate the festival demonstration honestly.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Keep spectacle and actual effects distinct; the humor comes from marketing, not unavoidable disasters.

npcs.name: Lady Serane Vell
npcs.description: A provincial ruler who delivers visible improvements while quietly making local institutions dependent on her patronage.
npcs.appearance: Immaculate cream clothes, a narrow silver circlet and an expression that changes only after others finish speaking.
npcs.personality: Disciplined, courteous and possessive; confuses gratitude with consent and loyalty with agreement.

speech.manner: Names shared interests before making an exact request.
speech.exampleLine: Independence is valuable. It still needs a roof.

npcs.background: Inherited unstable estates and restored public works through personal funding. Learned to treat every dependency as insurance against another crisis.

motivations.desire: Keep a reform council inside her sphere of influence.
motivations.fear: Losing authority after investing her identity in being indispensable.

offer.provides: Patronage, introductions and access to estate records.
offer.wantsInReturn: Public acknowledgment and a continuing place in decisions.

relationships: A council representative wants independent revenue.
Her steward worries about promises exceeding income.

secret.truth: She sponsors an opposition pamphlet to monitor its contributors.
clues: The printer's invoices use an estate intermediary.
Pamphlet drafts echo phrases from private council notes.
discoveryPaths: Follow the public printing accounts.
Speak to the intermediary about editorial instructions.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She remembers a visitor's earlier request and asks what it would cost now.

socialResponses.respect: Makes a useful offer with explicit strings.
socialResponses.pressure: Remains courteous while narrowing access.
socialResponses.betrayal: Withdraws favors and promotes a more dependable intermediary.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Offer the council a grant tied to an advisory seat.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Let her reforms be real; control grows from something people genuinely value.

npcs.name: Corvin Paleacre
npcs.description: An estate steward balancing a demanding household's image against the needs of people who actually keep it running.
npcs.appearance: An old formal coat, prematurely gray hair and a ledger carried in a weatherproof sleeve.
npcs.personality: Reliable, cautious and exhausted; smooths over conflict until others mistake silence for agreement.

speech.manner: Lists practical constraints without raising his voice.
speech.exampleLine: It can be arranged. Something else will then remain undone.

npcs.background: Rose from stable clerk to steward during a family's decline. Protecting the estate's workers now competes with maintaining its prestige.

motivations.desire: Fund necessary repairs before another ceremonial expense.
motivations.fear: Being replaced by someone who treats workers as disposable.

offer.provides: Estate access, employment context and introductions to household staff.
offer.wantsInReturn: A feasible proposal and discretion about individual workers.

relationships: A housekeeper trusts him with shortages.
The heir wants a lavish public celebration.

secret.truth: He has been quietly selling nonessential family ornaments to cover wages.
clues: Display cases have convincing substitutes.
A broker's invoices match pay dates.
discoveryPaths: Compare household inventories with auction records.
Ask Corvin how he kept wages current.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He changes a seating plan to accommodate a tired servant.

socialResponses.respect: Explains the household's actual limits.
socialResponses.pressure: Requests written priorities so tradeoffs become visible.
socialResponses.betrayal: Stops unofficial favors and informs affected staff.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Present a repair budget to the family together with the housekeeper.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: He manages one estate, not unlimited wealth or automatic access to its owners.

npcs.name: Ilsa Riverglass
npcs.description: An envoy seeking a workable border agreement while questioning the mandate her own superiors gave her.
npcs.appearance: Travel-worn blue silk, a plain pin representing her office and a case of carefully sorted correspondence.
npcs.personality: Poised, curious and guarded; advocates listening while withholding the parts of her position she doubts.

speech.manner: Restates an opposing concern before answering.
speech.exampleLine: Before we agree on a border, whom are we asking to live with it?

npcs.background: Spent years translating disputes between settlements. Her first major appointment has a deadline incompatible with meaningful consultation.

motivations.desire: Reach an agreement residents can live with.
motivations.fear: Being praised for an accord that harms people absent from the room.

offer.provides: Official introductions, negotiation context and access to public proposals.
offer.wantsInReturn: Accurate messages and consent before attributing statements.

relationships: A superior wants quick signatures.
A local organizer asks for time to consult residents.

secret.truth: She has authority to extend the talks but has not disclosed it.
clues: Her commission includes an unused extension clause.
A secretary has reserved rooms beyond the public deadline.
discoveryPaths: Read the published terms of her commission.
Ask the secretary why the extra rooms were booked.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She asks an overlooked attendant how the proposed change affects their road home.

socialResponses.respect: Shares the limits and flexibility of her mandate.
socialResponses.pressure: Sticks to documented positions and consults affected people.
